To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystallization of ultrathin layers of PEO in a multilayer assembly results in a single, high-asper-ratio lamella morphology that is highly ordered and that the crystallization habit of these ultrathin layers imparts two orders-of-magnitude reduction in gas permeability.

the crystallization of polyethylene oxide (a polymer with a high degree of crystallinity) can be confined to a single layer, and that the crystallization habit of this layer imparts two orders-of-magnitude reduction in the gas-permeability of the layer assembly.

the crystallization of ultrathin polyethylene oxide (U-PEO) layers in nanolayer assemblies is a unique process that produces high-aspect-ratum lamellae that reduce the permeability by two orders of magnitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of polymer-based nanomaterials and the study of their structure-property relationships.
the fabrication of ultrathigh aspect ratio polymer nanolayers and the discovery of the unique morphology that emerges as the thickness of the PEO layers is confined to 10 nanometers.
the fabrication of ultrathim polymer layers and the crystallization of polymeric materials in confined environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the confinement of PEO layers to 20 nm thickness induces a crystallization habit that is distinct from that of bulk PEO, resulting in a dramatic reduction in the gas diffusion coefficient.
we have discovered a new crystallization habit of PEO that is unique to nanoscale confinement, and this new morphology is responsible for the observed gas barrier properties.
the confinement of the PEO layers leads to a unique crystallization morphology that is responsible for the dramatic reduction in gas transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel approach to the fabrication of polymer multilayer assemblies and have discovered a new morphology that arises when polymer chains are confined within a few nanometers of the surface.
we have developed a novel process to make ultrathin polymer nanolayer assemblies and discovered a unique crystalline morphology in the confined layers.
we discovered a morphology of single, high-asymmetry crystallites in a polymer nanolayer assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of a polymer crystallized in a confined geometry can be tuned by the thickness of the layer.
nanolayered structures can be engineered to control crystallization and to impart new properties.
the confinement of the crystallizable polymer to nanolayers is a powerful tool that can be exploited to tailor the structure, properties, and performance of polymer-based materials.
